definitions.explanation: Accepting something unpleasant or difficult without resistance. Implies willingly or resignedly enduring hardship, punishment, or unfavorable circumstances.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}を{甘受|かんじゅ}する。
{批判|ひはん}は{甘受|かんじゅ}しなければならない。
{自分|じぶん}の{選択|せんたく}の{結果|けっか}である{以上|いじょう}、この{不便|ふべん}さは{甘受|かんじゅ}するしかない。
examples.english: Since this is the result of my own choice, I have no choice but to accept this inconvenience.

notes:
{甘受|かんじゅ} means accepting something unpleasant without resistance. It implies resignation or willingness to endure hardship.

KANJI NOTE:
The character {甘|かん} here means "willingly" or "contentedly," not its more common meaning of "sweet."

COMMON OBJECTS (always negative):
- {批判|ひはん}を{甘受|かんじゅ}する: to accept criticism
- {処分|しょぶん}を{甘受|かんじゅ}する: to accept punishment
- {不利益|ふりえき}を{甘受|かんじゅ}する: to accept disadvantage
- {結果|けっか}を{甘受|かんじゅ}する: to accept consequences

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept (neutral; broader use)
- {我慢|がまん}する: to endure, put up with (focuses on the suffering)
- {諦|あきら}める: to give up, resign oneself (focuses on abandoning hope)

REGISTER:
Formal and literary. Common in written Japanese, legal contexts, and serious discussion. Rarely used in casual conversation.
